primitives.name: Corrected Forecast Combination
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Two-step correction:** f^{CZZ}_{T+h|T} = f^{ZZ}_{T+h|T} + γ·e^{ZZ}_{T|T-h}, ZZ ∈ {EW, BG/OLS-optimal, any}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f^{CZZ}_{T+h|T}': 'corrected combined forecast at time T+h given information up to T, unitless', 'f^{ZZ}_{T+h|T}': 'uncorrected combined forecast, unitless', 'e^{ZZ}_{T|T-h}': 'combined forecast error at T given forecast at T-h, unitless', 'γ': 'correction weight, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Individual forecasts are unbiased; combined errors exhibit serial correlation; stationarity of ARMA process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When combined errors are not serially correlated (ACF(1) < 0.15), correction offers no benefit.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that forecast combination errors often display serial correlation, violating standard independence assumptions. This allows for a two-step correction: first, compute the combined forecast; second, adjust it by a fraction γ of the prior combined error. Theoretically, this leads to conditional MSE dominance due to reduced residual variance. The GLS approach extends this by jointly estimating weights and correction parameters under an ARMA error model, offering a principled method to optimize both components simultaneously. The correction term γ·e^{ZZ}_{T|T-h} acts as a feedback mechanism that leverages past performance to improve future predictions. If γ is fixed at 0.5, it provides a robust default strategy. However, estimation introduces additional variance unless the signal-to-noise ratio is strong. The conditional error model further refines this by modeling the expected error as a function of past errors, enabling more nuanced uncertainty quantification. These primitives together enable a dual framework: one for static correction and another for dynamic optimization under temporal dependence.
